title: Detection of degradation of magnetic resonance (MR) images: comparison of an automated MR image-quality analysis system with trained human observers
reader_subset_verified: no human readers found at appraisal
rob_patient_selection_evidence: Parameters for imaging the test object and normal human volunteers were set to values that decreased the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), caused distortion, and increased the slice thickness and separation.
rob_patient_selection_rationale: Abstract only; volunteers and a test object are mentioned but no sampling rule, number of subjects, or inclusion/exclusion criteria are described.
rob_index_test_evidence: To evaluate the validity of this assumption, we compared the sensitivity of a test object and automated image analysis system for MR imaging QC with the sensitivity of trained human observers
rob_index_test_rationale: No statement about whether observers were blinded to which images had been degraded or to the degradation level, and no pre-specified detection threshold is reported.
rob_reference_standard_evidence: with the sensitivity of trained human observers by evaluating images that were intentionally degraded
rob_reference_standard_rationale: The ground truth was the experimentally applied degradation, which is known by construction and therefore classifies the target condition (presence/level of degradation) correctly.
rob_flow_timing_rationale: The abstract gives no information on how many images or observers entered the analysis, or whether any data were excluded.
app_patient_selection_evidence: Parameters for imaging the test object and normal human volunteers were set to values that decreased the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), caused distortion, and increased the slice thickness and separation.
app_patient_selection_rationale: A phantom test object plus normal volunteers, with no clinical brain-MRI patient population, does not match a review question about preserving diagnostic content in patients.
app_index_test_evidence: Automated analysis of test object images was able to detect all image degradations at the minimum levels applied.
app_index_test_rationale: The index test is deliberate parameter-driven degradation assessed by an automated QC system, not an accelerated or AI-based image reconstruction.
app_reference_standard_evidence: Further investigation is needed to better define the accuracy with which quantitative image-quality analysis predicts the effects of degraded image quality on the ability of human observers to detect subtle abnormalities in clinical images.
app_reference_standard_rationale: The authors explicitly state that the link between image-quality degradation and detection of clinical abnormalities was not established, so the reference does not address diagnostic content.
rater_status: verified
consensus_note: Independently appraised by three reviewers (2026-08-06); independent ratings agreed on all domains, no adjudication required.
